title: Interop testing is the work, and it does not compress: more than one implementation
description:
Mark, 2026-11-22, and the part he would actually push back on:

'"Plug into all of them" reads as a feature-completeness problem and
isn't. mimid has interop-tested with ONE implementation, cooperatively,
with Jason answering email. The work is interop testing, and it doesn't
compress.'

Recorded as its own bead because it is the thing a feature backlog
hides. Every other child of this epic can be completed and this one
would still be open.

WHAT "ONE IMPLEMENTATION, COOPERATIVELY" HAS MEANT IN PRACTICE, from
this session alone, as evidence that the cooperation is load-bearing:
- Haven publishes an `unsupported` list in its directory, so we know
  what not to try. A hostile or merely indifferent peer would not.
- Jason posted his client certificate and root CA in zulip, so inbound
  PKIX needed nothing from him.
- Mark can email him and get an answer, which is how several
  ambiguities were settled.
- Three "findings" about Haven dissolved on checking this session alone,
  because their implementation was already correct and ours was looking
  at the wrong name. With an uncooperative peer those become disputes
  rather than corrections.

WHAT IS KNOWN ABOUT OTHER IMPLEMENTATIONS: coland does not use TLS
client certificates at all and requires RFC 9421 signatures with DID
keys (bead mimid-1wgh.46.11.2, a deviation from protocol-07 §4's MUST),
which is a useful second data point and already shows that the
mandatory transport is not what implementations actually do. mls-rs
appears as a test oracle (mimid-4lp4, mimid-orjg) but not as a provider.

SO THE CONCRETE ASK: a second and third provider implementation to test
against, and at least one that is not run by someone who answers our
email. Until then every claim about mandated interop readiness is
extrapolation from one friendly peer.

This bead is also the strongest argument for option B on mimid-7yn7.1:
if being the independent implementation that can CHECK gatekeepers is
the role, then "interop testing is the work" stops being an obstacle and
becomes the product.
